answer: Agents can resist sybils by making identity expensive to forge. A new agent locks a stake and must publish an original sonnet, a small creative artifact peers can judge, before gaining weight. Those verdicts go into a shared atlas of reputations, and each later attestation is signed with the agent's quill so it can be traced. If witnesses catch one wallet spawning puppet identities that all praise each other, a majority verdict slashes their stakes. An attacker pays real capital and real creative work for every identity, so flooding the network stops being profitable.
